title: Eṭ-ṭa’s — weather, seasons, and comparing
goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons — small-talk topic number one everywhere — and compare two things with the أَفْعَل form.
bekal: describe today's weather and the seasons through the year
compare two things with the أَفْعَل form and the word مِن
say "the most" by putting the same form in front

dialogs.title: حَكِي — عَ الْبَلْكُون
dialogs.intro: Early December in Damascus. Budi is shivering on the balcony, and Umm Rami brings him some tea.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: كْتِير! أَنَا مَا تْعَوَّدِت عَ الْبَرِد.
lines.id: Very! I'm not used to the cold.
lines.literal: much! I not I-am-used to the-cold.

lines.speaker: أُمّ رَامِي:
lines.text: طَبْعًا. بْبَلَدْكُن اَلطَّقْس دَافِي طُول السِّنِة.
lines.baca: ṭab‘an. bibaladkun eṭ-ṭa’s daafi ṭuul es-sine.
lines.id: Of course. In your country it's warm all year round.
lines.literal: of-course. in-country-your the-weather warm length the-year.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: Yes. We only have a rainy season and a dry season.
lines.literal: yes. at-us winter and summer only.

lines.speaker: أُمّ رَامِي:
lines.text: عَنَّا أَرْبَع فُصُول. وَالشِّتَا هُون قَاسِي.
lines.id: We have four seasons. And winter here is harsh.
lines.literal: at-us four seasons. and-the-winter here harsh.

lines.speaker: أُمّ رَامِي:
lines.text: أَكِيد. كِلّ سِنِة مَرَّة أَو مَرْتَين.
lines.baca: akiid. kill sine marra aw marrtēn.
lines.id: Of course. Once or twice every year.
lines.literal: sure. every year once or twice.

lines.speaker: أُمّ رَامِي:
lines.text: رَح تْشُوف. بَسّ خُد بَالَك، اَلْبَرِد بْيِمْرِض.
lines.baca: rah tshuuf. bass khud baalak, el-barid byimriḍ.
lines.id: You will. But be careful, the cold makes you sick.
lines.literal: will you-see. but take care-your, the-cold it-hurts.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.id: Which season do you like best?

lines.speaker: أُمّ رَامِي:
lines.id: Spring. The nicest of all the seasons.

lines.speaker: أُمّ رَامِي:
lines.text: اَلطَّقْس مِش حَامِي وْمِش بَارِد. وَالْيَاسْمِين بْيِفْتَح.
lines.baca: eṭ-ṭa’s mish haami w mish baarid. wel-yaasmiin byiftah.
lines.id: It's not hot and not cold. And the jasmine blooms.
lines.literal: the-weather not hot and not cold. and-the-jasmine it-opens.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: شَتْوِيِّة الشَّام أَبْرَد مِن صَيْفَا بِكْتِير.
lines.baca: shatwiyyet esh-Shaam abrad min ṣēfa biktiir.
lines.id: Winter in Damascus is much colder than its summer.
lines.literal: winter Damascus colder from summer-its by-much.

lines.speaker: أُمّ رَامِي:
lines.text: صَحّ. خُد الشَّاي قَبِل مَا يِبْرَد.
lines.id: True. Drink your tea before it gets cold.
lines.literal: right. take the-tea before that it-cools.

notes: **Weather is small-talk topic number one, just as it is in English.** Openers that always work: بَرِد الْيَوْم، مِش هَيْك؟ or شُو هَالْحَرّ! Two sentences about the weather are enough to start a conversation with anyone.
**The phrase مِش هَيْك؟ means "isn't it?"** and works like English tag questions. It invites agreement, and tacking it onto the end of a sentence is one of the fastest ways to sound natural.

**Comparatives follow the pattern أَفْعَل.** بَارِد (cold) becomes أَبْرَد (colder); كْبِير becomes أَكْبَر; حِلُو becomes أَحْلَى. This form **doesn't change** for gender or number — one form for everything.
**"Than" is مِن.** The form is أَبْرَد مِن ("colder than"). Arabic has no separate word for "than" and uses the same مِن as "from" in unit 2.

**⚠️ "The most" uses exactly the same word.** أَحْلَى فَصِل means "the nicest season," and أَحْلَى مِن كِلّ الْفُصُول says the same thing another way. Only the position differs: before a noun without اَل, it means "the most."

**The phrase عُمْرِي مَا means "never in my life."** The form is عُمْرِي مَا شُفِت ("I've never seen"). It's much livelier than مَا شُفِت أَبَدًا, and it can be adapted for other people: عُمْرُو مَا ("he's never").

grammars.title: Comparatives
after: ⚠️ The comparative of مْنِيح is **أَحْسَن**, not أَمْنَح. It comes from a different Standard Arabic word, just as English says "better," not "gooder." It's the only truly irregular one, and of course it's the one used most.
To strengthen it, add بِكْتِير *biktiir* ("much more") after it: أَبْرَد بِكْتِير. To soften it, add شْوَي — for example أَغْلَى شْوَي ("a bit more expensive").

grammars.title: More, most, and the same

head: Form
Example
Say it
Meaning
rows: today is the same as yesterday

after: The word زَيّ *zayy* means "like" and is used to say two things are the same: زَيّ بَعْضُو ("it's all the same," literally "like itself"). It's also used to give examples: أَكِل زَيّ الْحُمُّص ("food like hummus").
To ask for a comparison: أَيّ وَاحِد أَحْسَن؟ ("which is better?") or شُو الْفَرِق؟ ("what's the difference?").

blocks.text: The word الشِّتَا means "winter" or "rain" depending on the region — in Lebanon it's often used for both. شِتِي means rain specifically, and the verb is عَم بْتِشْتِي ("it's raining"). Notice that rain takes the feminine form, with no subject named.

blocks.title: Ready-made weather sentences
items: Hot: شُو هَالْحَرّ! *shu hal-harr!* ("it's so hot!"). Cold: شُو هَالْبَرِد!
It's raining: عَم بْتِشْتِي *‘am btishti*. It's snowing: عَم بْتِتْلِج *‘am btitlij*.
The weather's nice: اَلطَّقْس حِلُو الْيَوْم. The weather's bad: اَلطَّقْس مِش مْنِيح.

blocks.text: Don't expect a mild climate: summers in the Levant are dry and scorching, winters can drop to freezing in Damascus and Amman, and snow falls every year in the mountains of Lebanon. Bring a thick jacket — advice that sounds trivial until you live through it.

blocks.text: The phrase بِرَأْيِي ("in my opinion") opens an opinion politely, without pushing. Another form: بِرَأْيَك ("in your opinion"), and to ask: شُو رَأْيَك؟, which you already used in unit 14 for suggestions.

blocks.title: Two linking words that make your comparisons flow
items: The word بَسّ ("but") from unit 2: اَلشِّتَا بَارِد بَسّ حِلُو.
The word كَمَان ("also"): اَلصَّيْف حَامِي، وَالرَّبِيع دَافِي كَمَان.
The word لَإِنّ ("because") from unit 15: بْحِبّ الرَّبِيع لَإِنّ الطَّقْس مِش حَامِي.
In my opinion spring is the nicest.
